intro_notes: NOTE: You will need access to a car or truck and its owner's manual to meet some requirements for this merit badge. If you do not have your own vehicle, you should work with your counselor or other trusted adult to obtain access to a vehicle and the owner's manual for that vehicle.
NOTE: The official merit badge pamphlets are now free and downloadable HERE or can be purchased at the Scout Shop.

requirements.lead_text: Safety and Registration. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Safety and Registration. Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the hazards you are most likely to encounter during automotive maintenance activities, and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, or lessen these hazards. (b) Discuss with your counselor the safety equipment, tools, and clothing used while checking or repairing a motor vehicle. Use this equipment, tools, and/or clothing (when needed or called for) in meeting the requirements for this merit badge. (c) Explain the different ways motor vehicles are powered. (d) Explain the safety considerations when performing maintenance on a vehicle equipped with a high-voltage electrical system. (e) Review the maintenance chart in the vehicle owner's manual. Explain the requirements and time limits. (f) Explain the purpose, importance, and limitations of safety belts and passive restraints. (g) Find out the requirements for your state's emissions and safety inspections (as applicable), including how often a vehicle needs to be inspected. (h) Explain the importance of registering a vehicle and find out the annual registration fee for renewing your family car's registration.

Step 3 - Verify Mandatory Air bag Equipment: Air bags are required on all new passenger vehicles sold in the United States (p. 20).
Step 4 - Detect Rapid Crash Deceleration: If a front-end crash occurs, sensors in the air bags notice that the car has suddenly slowed down or even stopped (a process called deceleration) (p. 20).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: You are preparing to crawl beneath a vehicle to inspect the exhaust and suspension for Automotive Maintenance Requirement 1. Which safety procedure is strictly required before anyone goes under the car?
quiz_item.question: You are preparing to crawl beneath a vehicle to inspect the exhaust and suspension for Automotive Maintenance Requirement 1. Which safety procedure is strictly required before anyone goes under the car?
options: A. Raise one corner of the bumper with the emergency scissor jack from the trunk, leave the transmission in neutral, and crawl underneath immediately.
B. Keep the engine running inside a closed garage to warm the fluids while supporting the frame on hollow concrete cinder blocks.

C. Park on a firm level surface, set the parking brake, chock the wheels, lift the vehicle at manufacturer-specified jack points, and lower it onto rated mechanical jack stands before going underneath.
D. Stack wooden two-by-fours on top of a hydraulic floor jack saddle and rely on the hydraulic cylinder pressure alone to hold the vehicle up.

Complete Vehicle Lighting Circuits: The lighting system includes the interior overhead lights, instrument lights, headlights, taillights, turn signals, warning lights, hazard lights (p. 69).

step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Trigger Door Plunger Switch: When you open a car door, plunger-type switches close a circuit to the interior lights and make them (p. 69).
Step 2 - Depress Pedal Brake Switch: When you apply the brakes, a switch under the pedal closes a circuit to the brake light bulbs so they light (p. 69).
Step 3 - Supply Battery Power Accessories: Wires connect the battery to many other accessories, including the sound system, heating and cooling systems, and (if the car has them) power (p. 69).
Step 4 - Turn Ignition Switch: In some cases (such as the sound system and the heating and cooling systems), you must also turn the ignitions witch on to close the circuit (p. 69).

pamphlet_excerpts: Bicycle Gear Ratio Analogy: You may have seen this idea at work on a bicycle (p. 33).
Low-Gear Hill-Climbing Torque: If your chain is on a small chain ring in the front and a large sprocket in the back, it will help you climb a very steep hill (p. 33).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: You are preparing to crawl beneath a vehicle to inspect the exhaust and suspension for Automotive Maintenance Requirement 1. Which safety procedure is strictly required before anyone goes under the car?
options: A. Raise one corner of the bumper with the emergency scissor jack from the trunk, leave the transmission in neutral, and crawl underneath immediately.
B. Keep the engine running inside a closed garage to warm the fluids while supporting the frame on hollow concrete cinder blocks.

C. Park on a firm level surface, set the parking brake, chock the wheels, lift the vehicle at manufacturer-specified jack points, and lower it onto rated mechanical jack stands before going underneath.
D. Stack wooden two-by-fours on top of a hydraulic floor jack saddle and rely on the hydraulic cylinder pressure alone to hold the vehicle up.
choices: A. Raise one corner of the bumper with the emergency scissor jack from the trunk, leave the transmission in neutral, and crawl underneath immediately.

C. Park on a firm level surface, set the parking brake, chock the wheels, lift the vehicle at manufacturer-specified jack points, and lower it onto rated mechanical jack stands before going underneath.
D. Stack wooden two-by-fours on top of a hydraulic floor jack saddle and rely on the hydraulic cylinder pressure alone to hold the vehicle up.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Park on a firm level surface, set the parking brake, chock the wheels, lift the vehicle at manufacturer-specified jack points, and lower it onto rated mechanical jack stands before going underneath.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Hydraulic jacks can fail or leak pressure without warning; a vehicle must always be supported on properly rated mechanical jack stands on level ground with wheels chocked before anyone works beneath it.
